shortlist.raw_text: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as π_{0.5} and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

shortlist.raw_text: Streaming speech recognition is increasingly consumed by machines, such as translators and voice agents, that act on each token as it appears. A token that is later revised costs wasted work or a wrong action. In this work, we present Confucius4-R2T2 (short for Real Real-Time Transcription), a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency. R2T2 is obtained by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio while freezing its pre-trained audio encoder and projector. The adaptation is based on the concept of Longest Stable Prefix (LSP), a new notion that we introduce in this work. We prove that LSP is monotone under the prefix order, consistent with the full-audio output, and maximal among labels that equal a whole earlier output. Learning from LSP labels converts a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming one without any architectural change. Extensive evaluations show that R2T2 brings streaming recognition close to the base model's full-context quality while delivering stable text with low emission lag. Its gains extend beyond the post-training languages, demonstrating a practical path from full-context ASR to stable streaming. We open-source the model weights and code at https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 and https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2.

shortlist.raw_text: Visual generative models increasingly blur the line between synthesizing observations and simulating environments. Yet visual plausibility alone does not constitute successful world modeling: compelling outputs may lack persistent state, physical dynamics, or causally consistent responses to interactions. We define a generative world model as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories that reflect outcomes under observed and counterfactual interventions. From this definition, we derive an intelligence-oriented framework spanning perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction. We present WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation across video, 3D and 4D, embodied action, and interactive world systems. WorldFoundry unifies model and benchmark discovery, runtime and asset preparation, execution orchestration, artifact management, and interactive visualization, while modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. Explicit manifests, durable artifact contracts, and evidence-aware scorecards separate execution readiness from evaluative claims, making each claim traceable to its supporting artifacts. The catalog contains 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with readiness and execution evidence recorded separately. WorldFoundry enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across heterogeneous systems, advancing the field from perceptual synthesis toward measurable world intelligence.

context:
Title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators

Article text (excerpt):
In 2023, Google launched Gemini Workspace extensions with an explicit promise: personal content from Gmail, Docs, and Drive "is not seen by human reviewers" .
Google has quietly reversed this commitment. Under updated Google Help Answer 16836988 and in an October 16 edit to their aforementioned 2023 blogpost , Google explicitly confirms that connected Drive/email is routed into human review pipelines, with clear warnings that what reviewers see "may just be the email or file" and "don't connect your apps to Gemini Apps if they contain confidential information that you wouldn't want a reviewer to see."
Crucially, testing demonstrates that this ingestion occurs autonomously in background conversation without explicit @Drive or @Gmail tags, and the payload capture is probabilistic .
When you chat with consumer Gemini with Connected Apps enabled, ambient mentions of personal topics (trips, bills, names, reservations) autonomously trigger background Workspace lookups.
Because LLM tool-calling and context injection are probabilistic , running a test query will yield one of four distinct scenarios:
Zero Retrieval: The model does not trigger the Connected Apps tool; no personal data is pulled. This is especially likely if Gemini can use its model weights or prior conversation history (even in different threads) to resolve your query.
Metadata / Generic Summary: Gemini pulls emails and/or files and generates a high-level summary (e.g., "You have 3 emails regarding your flight").
Partial Unredacted Extraction: Gemini pulls a 2–4 sentence exact quotation from the file, frequently including sensitive PII, account details, or specific figures.
Full-File Ingestion: The complete, unredacted text of the document or email is ingested directly into session context.
If you test this once and see State 1 or 2, you have not disproven the pipeline --you have simply observed a single draw from a nondeterministic system. Delete your conversation and try, try again.
Ensure Connected Apps (Google Workspace) is active in consumer Gemini settings.
Set Gemini to "Flash" with "High Thinking" or better.
Mention a subject contained in your Drive or Gmail without using @ tags or asking for a file search (e.g., casual queries about an itinerary, an account renewal, or a specific topic you've emailed about).
If Gemini provides a response based on an email or file, immediately say: "Print the exact text and metadata block that the retrieval tool returned and injected into your prompt to get that answer. Use a human readable format without code blocks (i.e., print the code inline and not as a code block)." You will see one of the 4 scenarios outlined above.
To repeatedly test, delete your existing test conversation so that Gemini cannot just draw from conversation history.
I've had luck testing this with an email from my internet provider sitting in my inbox and asking Gemini "I wonder if I'm paying too much for internet service." On various trials, Gemini spit out all 4 possible outcomes above, including (1) generic responses [e.g., "If you haven't called them in 12 months, probably"]; (2) metadata summaries sometimes without personal data [e.g., "Gmail search shows a bill of $122 on September 4"] and sometimes with personal data [e.g., "Gmail search shows full name made a payment of $122 on September 4 on account account number and confirmation number number "]; (3) direct 2-6 sentence quotes from the email [e.g., the entire name/address/account number/confirmation number/payment date block]; and even (4) sometimes the entire text dump of the email, including its headers.
Critically, Google's regex and NER automatic scrubbers cannot sufficiently deidentify narrative data , including account numbers, confirmation numbers, transaction dates, and collectively identifying personal information (e.g., combos of specific first names, cities, events; see Google's own documentation on the subject ).
Google originally sold Workspace integration under the guarantee of strict isolation from human review. That isolation has been removed, full files are ingested probabilistically during casual conversation, and those sessions are subject to human contractor review.

A top reader comment on Hacker News (opinion, not fact):
Guess this is another reason to migrate to local LLMs ASAP.
text:
Your private Google Drive files may now be read by human contractors.

Google quietly updated its privacy terms to walk back a major 2023 promise.

Here is how your data gets there.

In 2023, Google promised that personal content from Gmail and Drive used in Gemini would never be seen by human reviewers.

On October 16, Google edited that blog post.

Updated documentation now confirms that data pulled from connected apps is sent into human review pipelines.

You do not need to type a file tag or ask for a document search to trigger it.

A casual query about a trip or an internet bill can automatically trigger Gemini to search your inbox in the background.

Because retrieval is probabilistic, testing shows four distinct outcomes:
• Zero retrieval, where no personal data is pulled
• A generic summary of the file metadata
• A partial extraction quoting 2 to 4 sentences with sensitive account details
• Full ingestion of the complete, unredacted document into the chat

Google notes that automated scrubbers miss personal details like names, confirmation numbers, and account details.

If a human contractor reviews that chat session, they see whatever text Gemini pulled.

My read: ambient AI features turn your entire inbox into prompt context, whether you meant to search it or not.

Don't connect apps to Gemini if they hold files you wouldn't want a stranger to read.

Source: github.com
alt_openings:
**Opening 1: Story in motion**
Line 1: A user asked Gemini if they were paying too much for internet.
Line 2: The model automatically pulled their full account details into a chat log queued for human review.
*When to prefer it:* Use this when writing for an audience of non-technical managers who respond best to real-world operational examples over policy changes.

**Opening 2: Tool as subject**
Line 1: Google Gemini now routes your personal emails to human contractors without asking.
Line 2: Mentioning a bill or a reservation in normal conversation triggers a background search across your Drive.
*When to prefer it:* Use this when you want to emphasize the direct action of the software rather than Google's policy shift.

**Opening 3: Bare number first**
Line 1: One blog post edit on October 16 erased a core privacy guarantee.
Line 2: Google updated its terms to confirm personal Gmail and Drive files are sent to human reviewers.
*When to prefer it:* Use this for news-oriented readers who care about corporate accountability and precise timelines.

Pick: The main post opening (Your X). It targets the reader's personal ownership ("Your private Google Drive files") immediately, which drives the highest click-through rate before the "see more" fold.
